```{r go code}


aa <- c("A","R","N","D","C","E","Q","G","H","I",
        "L","K","M","F","P","S","T","W","Y","V","*")

# Read input file (adjust header=TRUE if needed)
library_info <- read.table("20240527_domainome_WT_screen_400-600_FINAL.txt",
                sep = "\t", header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

```{r complete library making}
complete_library <- library_info %>%
  crossing(replacement = aa) %>%
  rowwise() %>%  
  mutate(V3_mut = gsub("X", replacement, V3, fixed = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%  # reset rowwise grouping
  mutate(variant_ID = paste0(V2, "_", replacement)) %>%
  select(variant_ID, everything())

print(complete_library)

```

```{r to report the count of  designed variants and the non-designed }

complete_library_rep <- complete_library %>%
  mutate(V3_mut = gsub("\\*$", "", V3_mut))

dimsum_rep <- dimsum %>%
  mutate(aa_seq = gsub("\\*$", "", aa_seq))



dimsum_rep <- dimsum_rep %>%
  mutate(
    design_status = if_else(aa_seq %in% complete_library_rep$V3_mut, "Designed", "Non-designed")
  )

# 1️⃣ Number of variants by type
variant_counts <- dimsum_rep %>%
  group_by(design_status) %>%
  summarise(num_variants = n())

# 2️⃣ Sum of mean_count (replace with the correct column if needed)
count_summary <- dimsum_rep %>%
  group_by(design_status) %>%
  summarise(total_mean_count = sum(mean_count, na.rm = TRUE))

# 3️⃣ Combine both summaries
report_table <- left_join(variant_counts, count_summary, by = "design_status")

report_table

report_table <- report_table %>%
  mutate(
    frac_variants = num_variants / sum(num_variants),
    frac_counts = total_mean_count / sum(total_mean_count)
  )



# Define your sets
designed <- unique(complete_library_rep$V3_mut)
observed <- unique(dimsum_rep$aa_seq)

# Calculate overlap
intersection <- intersect(designed, observed)

# Draw Venn diagram
venn.plot <- draw.pairwise.venn(
  area1 = length(designed),
  area2 = length(observed),
  cross.area = length(intersection),
  category = c("Designed variants", "Observed variants"),
  fill = c("skyblue", "orange"),
  lty = "blank",
  cex = 2,
  cat.cex = 1.5
)

# Plot it
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(venn.plot)

```

```{r creating a column for annoting wild type entries}


merged_dimsum <- merged_dimsum %>%
  mutate(
    # extract original AA (before the number)
    original_aa = str_match(variant_ID, "_([A-Z])\\d")[,2],
    
    # extract mutant AA (after the last underscore)
    mutant_aa   = str_extract(variant_ID, "(?<=_)[:upper:]+$"),
    
    # wild-type = mutant AA == original AA
    is_wildtype = mutant_aa == original_aa
  )

```

```{r annoting stop codon }
merged_dimsum <- merged_dimsum %>%
  mutate(
    has_stop_codon = str_detect(V3_mut, "\\*"),  # TRUE/FALSE if '*' exists
    stop_pos = ifelse(has_stop_codon,
                      str_locate(V3_mut, "\\*")[, 1],  # position of stop codon
                      NA_integer_)
  )
merged_dimsum <- merged_dimsum %>%
  mutate(
    stable_ID = str_extract(variant_ID, "^[^_]+")  # everything before first "_"
  )



```

```{r}
# 1️⃣ Extract position
t_test <- merged_dimsum %>%
  mutate(
    position = as.numeric(str_match(variant_ID, "_[A-Z](\\d+)")[,2])
  )

# 2️⃣ Compute WT fitness/sigma per stable_ID and position
wt_df <- t_test %>%
  filter(is_wildtype) %>%
  group_by(stable_ID, position) %>%
  summarise(
    fitness_wt = mean(fitness, na.rm = TRUE),
    sigma_wt   = mean(sigma, na.rm = TRUE),  # ⚠️ replace `sigma` with your SD col name if different
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3️⃣ Join WT info back to all variants
t_test <- t_test %>%
  left_join(wt_df, by = c("stable_ID", "position"))

# 4️⃣ Compute t-statistic and two-tailed p-value (df = 4 or use your replicate df)
t_test <- t_test %>%
  mutate(
    t_stat  = (fitness - fitness_wt) / sqrt(sigma^2 + sigma_wt^2),
    p_value = 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat), df = 4))
  )

# 5️⃣ Flag significant results (p < 0.05)
t_test <- t_test %>%
  mutate(significant = p_value < 0.05)

# 6️⃣ Inspect results
t_test %>%
  select(stable_ID, variant_ID, position, fitness, fitness_wt, sigma, sigma_wt, t_stat, p_value, significant) %>%
  head()
```

```{r}
t_test_plot <- t_test_plot %>%
  mutate(
    fitness = -fitness,
    fitness_wt = -fitness_wt,
    category = case_when(
      is_wildtype ~ "Wild Type",
      has_stop_codon ~ "Stop Codon",
      TRUE ~ "Mutant"
    ),
    color_group = case_when(
      category == "Wild Type" & !significant ~ "WT (blue)",
      category == "Wild Type" &  significant ~ "WT (black)",
      category == "Mutant"    & !significant ~ "Mutant (yellow)",
      category == "Mutant"    &  significant ~ "Mutant (orange)",
      category == "Stop Codon" & !significant ~ "Stop Codon (red)",
      category == "Stop Codon" &  significant ~ "Stop Codon (pink)"
    )
  )

# Scatter plot with inverted fitness and custom colors
ggplot(t_test_plot, 
       aes(x = fitness_wt, y = fitness, color = color_group)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5, shape = 16) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "WT (blue)" = "blue",
      "WT (black)" = "black",
      "Mutant (yellow)" = "yellow",
      "Mutant (orange)" = "orange",
      "Stop Codon (red)" = "red",
      "Stop Codon (violet)" = "violet"
    ),
    name = "Variant Type & Significance"
  ) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, 
              linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  labs(
    title = "Mutant vs Wild-Type Fitness (Inverted Scale)",
    x = "Wild-Type Fitness (Inverted)",
    y = "Mutant / Stop Codon Fitness (Inverted)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
print(t_test_plot)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1️⃣ Add a column for WT – Mutant fitness difference
t_test <- t_test %>%
  mutate(
    fitness_diff = fitness_wt - fitness  # difference between WT and variant
  )

# 2️⃣ Categorize variants
t_test <- t_test %>%
  mutate(
    category = case_when(
      is_wildtype ~ "Wild Type",
      has_stop_codon ~ "Stop Codon",
      TRUE ~ "Mutant"
    )
  )

# 3️⃣ Summarize statistics for each category
fitness_diff_summary <- t_test %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_diff = mean(fitness_diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_diff = median(fitness_diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_diff = sd(fitness_diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(fitness_diff_summary)

# 4️⃣ Bar plot of mean fitness difference (with SD error bars)
p_bar <- ggplot(fitness_diff_summary, aes(x = category, y = mean_diff, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_diff - sd_diff, ymax = mean_diff + sd_diff), width = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean (WT – Mutant) Fitness Difference per Variant Type",
    x = "Variant Type",
    y = "Mean Fitness Difference (WT – Variant)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

print(p_bar)

# 5️⃣ Violin plot of all fitness differences
p_violin <- ggplot(t_test, aes(x = category, y = fitness_diff, fill = category)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of (WT – Mutant) Fitness Differences",
    x = "Variant Type",
    y = "Fitness Difference (WT – Variant)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

print(p_violin)

# 6️⃣ Save the plots
ggsave("fitness_diff_barplot.png", plot = p_bar, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
ggsave("fitness_diff_violinplot.png", plot = p_violin, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

```{r PFAM ID add}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)

# 1️⃣ Count number of wild-types per Pfam
pfam_counts <- violin_wt %>%
  group_by(Pfam_ID) %>%
  summarise(num_variants = n(), .groups = "drop")

# 2️⃣ Keep only Pfams with >= 4 wild-types
valid_pfams <- pfam_counts %>%
  filter(num_variants >= 4) %>%
  pull(Pfam_ID)

violin_wt_filtered <- violin_wt %>%
  filter(Pfam_ID %in% valid_pfams)

# 3️⃣ Determine number of plots you want (for example, 5)
num_plots <- 5

# 4️⃣ Split Pfams almost evenly across plots
pfam_list <- unique(violin_wt_filtered$Pfam_ID)
chunks <- split(pfam_list, cut(seq_along(pfam_list), breaks = num_plots, labels = FALSE))

# 5️⃣ Function to plot one chunk of Pfams
plot_violin_chunk <- function(pfam_subset, chunk_num) {
  
  df_chunk <- violin_wt_filtered %>%
    filter(Pfam_ID %in% pfam_subset)
  
  p <- ggplot(df_chunk, aes(x = Pfam_ID, y = fitness, fill = Pfam_ID)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, color = "black", alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Wild-Type Fitness by Pfam ID (Set", chunk_num, ")"),
      x = "Pfam ID",
      y = "Fitness",
      fill = "Pfam ID"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 6),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    )
  
  # Save plot
  filename <- paste0("wildtype_fitness_violin_set_", chunk_num, ".png")
  ggsave(filename, plot = p, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)
  
  return(p)
}

# 6️⃣ Generate plots for all chunks
plots <- imap(chunks, plot_violin_chunk)

# 7️⃣ Display first plot as a check
plots[[1]]
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)

# 1️⃣ Filter Pfams with > 4 variants
pfam_counts <- violin_wt %>%
  group_by(Pfam_ID) %>%
  summarise(num_variants = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(num_variants > 4)

# Keep only these Pfams
violin_filtered <- violin_wt %>%
  filter(Pfam_ID %in% pfam_counts$Pfam_ID)

# 2️⃣ Split Pfams into chunks for multiple plots
num_plots <- 3  # You can adjust number of plots
pfam_list <- unique(violin_filtered$Pfam_ID)
pfam_chunks <- split(pfam_list, cut(seq_along(pfam_list), num_plots, labels = FALSE))

# 3️⃣ Generate a plot for each chunk
plots <- map2(pfam_chunks, seq_along(pfam_chunks), ~ {
  chunk_data <- violin_filtered %>% filter(Pfam_ID %in% .x)
  
  ggplot(chunk_data, aes(x = Pfam_ID, y = fitness, fill = Pfam_ID)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, color = "black", alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Wild-Type Fitness Distribution by Pfam (Plot", .y, ")"),
      x = "Pfam ID",
      y = "Fitness",
      fill = "Pfam ID"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    )
})

# 4️⃣ Display plots
plots[[1]]  # first plot
plots[[2]]  # second plot
plots[[3]]  # third plot (adjust based on num_plots)

# Optionally save each plot
walk2(plots, seq_along(plots), ~ ggsave(paste0("violin_wt_Pfam_plot_", .y, ".png"), plot = .x, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300))


```
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)

# 1️⃣ Filter Pfams with > 4 variants
pfam_counts <- violin_wt %>%
  group_by(Pfam_ID) %>%
  summarise(num_variants = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(num_variants > 4)

# Keep only these Pfams
violin_filtered <- violin_wt %>%
  filter(Pfam_ID %in% pfam_counts$Pfam_ID) %>%
  mutate(inverted_fitness = -fitness)  # invert fitness

# 2️⃣ Split Pfams into chunks for multiple plots
num_plots <- 3  # Adjust as needed
pfam_list <- unique(violin_filtered$Pfam_ID)
pfam_chunks <- split(pfam_list, cut(seq_along(pfam_list), num_plots, labels = FALSE))

# 3️⃣ Generate a plot for each chunk
plots <- map2(pfam_chunks, seq_along(pfam_chunks), ~ {
  chunk_data <- violin_filtered %>% filter(Pfam_ID %in% .x)
  
  ggplot(chunk_data, aes(x = Pfam_ID, y = inverted_fitness, fill = Pfam_ID)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, color = "black", alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Wild-Type Fitness Distribution by Pfam (Inverted, Plot", .y, ")"),
      x = "Pfam ID",
      y = "Inverted Fitness",
      fill = "Pfam ID"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    )
})

# 4️⃣ Display plots
plots[[1]]  # first plot
plots[[2]]  # second plot
plots[[3]]  # third plot (adjust based on num_plots)
```

```{r}

# Prepare plotting dataframe
t_test_plot <- t_test_neg %>%
  mutate(
    wt_minus_mut = fitness_wt - fitness,
    diff_category = case_when(
      wt_minus_mut == 0 ~ "Wild Type",
      wt_minus_mut < 0  ~ "Negative (mutant fitter than WT)",
      wt_minus_mut > 0  ~ "Positive (mutant less fit than WT)"
    ),
    color_group = case_when(
      diff_category == "Wild Type" & !significant ~ "WT (blue)",
      diff_category == "Wild Type" & significant  ~ "WT (black)",
      diff_category == "Negative (mutant fitter than WT)" & !significant ~ "Mutant (yellow)",
      diff_category == "Negative (mutant fitter than WT)" & significant ~ "Mutant (orange)",
      diff_category == "Positive (mutant less fit than WT)" & !significant ~ "Mutant (red)",
      diff_category == "Positive (mutant less fit than WT)" & significant ~ "Mutant (pink)"
    )
  )

# Scatter plot
ggplot(t_test_plot, aes(x = 0, y = wt_minus_mut, color = color_group)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5, shape = 16, position = position_jitter(width = 0.2)) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "WT (blue)" = "blue",
      "WT (black)" = "black",
      "Mutant (yellow)" = "yellow",
      "Mutant (orange)" = "orange",
      "Mutant (red)" = "red",
      "Mutant (pink)" = "pink"
    ),
    name = "Variant Type & Significance"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Fitness Difference Relative to Wild-Type",
    x = "Wild-Type Reference",
    y = "Fitness Difference (WT - Mutant)",
    caption = "Negative = mutant fitter than WT, Positive = mutant less fit than WT"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
`
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)

# 1️⃣ Filter only wild-type variants
wt_data <- t_test %>%
  filter(is_wildtype) %>%
  mutate(variant_label = variant_ID)

# Check number of wild types
num_wt <- nrow(wt_data)
cat("Total wild-type variants:", num_wt, "\n")

# 2️⃣ Split into chunks of 100 variants each
wt_chunks <- split(wt_data, ceiling(seq_along(1:nrow(wt_data)) / 100))

# 3️⃣ Function to make a violin plot for a chunk
plot_violin_chunk <- function(df, chunk_num) {
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = variant_label, y = fitness, fill = variant_label)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, color = "black", outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.5) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Wild-Type Fitness Distribution (Set", chunk_num, ")"),
      x = "Wild-Type Variant",
      y = "Fitness"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6)
    )
  
  # Save each plot
  #filename <- paste0("wildtype_fitness_violin_set_", chunk_num, ".png")
  #ggsave(filename, plot = p, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)
  
  return(p)
}

# 4️⃣ Generate and save all plots
plots <- imap(wt_chunks, plot_violin_chunk)

# Display the first plot
plots[[1]]
```

```{r}
# Install if not already installed
install.packages("patchwork")

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(patchwork)

# Subset wild-type variants
wt_variants <- t_test_plot %>%
  filter(is_wildtype) %>%
  mutate(group_id = str_sub(variant_ID, 1, 4))  # extract first 4 letters

# Get unique groups
groups <- unique(wt_variants$group_id)

# Create an empty list to store plots
plot_list <- list()

# Loop over each group and create a violin plot
for(g in groups){
  df_group <- wt_variants %>% filter(group_id == g)
  
  p <- ggplot(df_group, aes(x = variant_ID, y = fitness)) +
    geom_violin(fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, fill = "white", outlier.shape = NA) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Group ", g),
      x = "Variant ID",
      y = "Fitness"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )
  
  plot_list[[g]] <- p
}
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)

# Count significant mutations per domain and exclude zeros
sig_mutations_per_domain <- t_test %>%
  group_by(stable_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    num_significant = sum(significant, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(num_significant > 0)

# Split domains into chunks of 100
domain_list <- unique(sig_mutations_per_domain$stable_ID)
domain_chunks <- split(domain_list, ceiling(seq_along(domain_list)/100))

# Generate and save a plot for each chunk
plots <- map2(domain_chunks, seq_along(domain_chunks), ~ {
  chunk_data <- sig_mutations_per_domain %>%
    filter(stable_ID %in% .x)
  
  p <- ggplot(chunk_data, aes(x = reorder(stable_ID, -num_significant), y = num_significant)) +
    geom_col(fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Significant Mutations per Domain (Plot", .y, ")"),
      x = "Domain (stable_ID)",
      y = "Number of Significant Mutations (out of 21)"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:21, limits = c(0, 21)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    )
  
  # Save each plot
  ggsave(paste0("sig_mutations_per_domain_plot_", .y, ".png"), plot = p, width = 14, height = 6, dpi = 300)
  
  return(p)
})

plots[[1]]
```
